description: `total` is how many rows matched, not how many the page holds. LIMIT bounds delivery; it is the only thing an agent has to tell a first page from a whole answer, and a total clipped to the page size says: this is all of it, about every first page. These cases pin the count against a ground truth taken at a limit high enough that nothing pages at all. Two mechanisms had to change for that and each has its own case: the clause pipeline now reports its size before OFFSET and LIMIT cut it, and the running top-K trim counts the rows it discards on rank. The name-index streams are the third mechanism: they answer from the per-segment deduplicated row counts stored at overlay build time, and their cases ask a five-row page to carry the size of the whole corpus. The segment fetch cap that used to be the other such place is gone: a bare LIMIT is now trimmed by the same running top-K as an ordered one, because the pipeline sorts by (name, line, path, fql_kind) even with no ORDER BY, and the four cases in clause_pipeline.json that pinned the cap are enforced rather than expected to fail. Both mechanisms were checked by mutation rather than assumed: with the trim's count disabled the same query reads '1 of 2 shown' through the built binary on the sibling workspace and '1 of 8 shown' with it on, against an unlimited answer of 8. What no case here can see is whether the collapse that now runs before the trim is reached at all, because it is defined not to move answers; that was measured separately with a panic in place -- one ordinary query collapsed 8 of 108 row ids inside a single segment, before any of them was built -- and it is pinned by the unit tests in fast_paths/tests.rs, which do go red.

cases.name: the_answer_this_suite_measures_against
cases.description: Ground truth. A limit above TOPK_THRESHOLD (1000) arms no top-K, so every matching row is built and nothing is shed or truncated: seven functions in this corpus exceed 150 lines. Every total below is this seven.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: a_page_reports_the_size_of_the_answer_it_came_from
cases.description: LIMIT 2 over the same seven rows. Two rows come back and the count says seven. K * TOPK_OVER_FETCH is eight here, so the working set never reaches the trim's threshold and nothing is shed — this case isolates the pipeline's own count, taken before OFFSET and LIMIT rather than after them.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 2

cases.name: the_running_trim_counts_what_it_sheds
cases.description: The same seven rows at LIMIT 1, which puts K * TOPK_OVER_FETCH at four and so does arm the trim: the working set passes four while the segments are still being read and is cut back to two, three times over. Those discarded rows never reach the clause pipeline, so the pipeline's own count cannot see them and the trim has to hand back how many it dropped. Without that the answer here reads as four rows, or two — the size of a window nobody asked for. The rows are distinct because duplicates are collapsed before anything sheds; that is what makes them countable at all.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 1

cases.name: a_name_ordered_stream_counts_the_answer_it_streams_from
cases.description: The streams answer the count without the walk. `ORDER BY name [DESC]`, with at most an `fql_kind` equality beside it, streams the name FST in order and stops after LIMIT + OFFSET rows -- but every segment's deduplicated row count was stored when the overlay was built, and a kind-filtered stream's bitmap knows its own cardinality, so the total beside the streamed page is the corpus's answer, not the page. This shape used to be the last surviving member of the family this suite exists to kill -- an early exit that assumes LIMIT bounds the answer, reporting total: 5 on this corpus of 59636 rows -- and was pinned here as an expected failure until the stored counts closed it. Where those counts cannot speak for the answer, two segments built from one source path, the streams decline and the pipeline answers; the unit suites pin that decline.
cases.fql: FIND symbols ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 5

cases.name: a_bare_limit_answers_from_the_stream_with_the_same_total
cases.description: The shortest query an agent can type, served by the same ascending stream: with no ORDER BY written the pipeline's default ordering starts with name, so the page is the ORDER BY name page and the total is the same stored corpus count. Before the stream claimed this shape it materialised every row in the corpus to deliver five of them.

cases.name: the_pipeline_counts_the_same_corpus
cases.description: Ground truth for the two stream cases above, through a route no stream serves: a WHERE clause declines the name streams, and line >= 1 matches every row -- lines are 1-based -- so this is the full scan's collapsed count of the same corpus. If the stored per-segment counts and the pipeline's collapse ever disagree, the three cases split here.

cases.name: the_default_page_is_a_bound_the_engine_is_told_about
cases.description: No LIMIT written. The engine used to build every matching row and the twenty-row default was cut afterwards, so this query materialised rows up to the row budget to show twenty; the default page is now handed to the engine as the LIMIT an explicit `LIMIT 20` would carry, and it takes the same name stream. Twenty rows, and the total is the whole corpus -- the same 59636 the explicit-LIMIT stream and the pipeline report above -- because the bound changes what is held, never what is counted.

cases.name: the_default_page_under_a_predicate_rides_the_running_trim
cases.description: The same default page through the pipeline: a WHERE declines the name streams, so the bound arms the running top-K trim at twenty. Every row is still read and counted; only twenty are held. Same total as every other case on this corpus.
